# Understanding Cairns: A Summary

## The Pulse (Rule C1)
A pulse boosts a cairn's height by adding the stride plus bonus marks. The bonus is calculated by dividing the current height by the stride and rounding down—this tells you how many "complete stride units" fit into the current height. So a taller cairn gets more bonus marks from a pulse than a shorter one.

## Repeated Pulses (Rule C2)
When you apply multiple pulses in sequence, you must recalculate the bonus after each pulse based on the new height. You can't just multiply the effect of one pulse—the bonus changes as the height grows, so later pulses often add more than earlier ones.

## Leaks (Rule C3)
A leak removes marks after each pulse. The amount lost is calculated by dividing the pulsed height by the leak value and rounding down. The leak operates on the new height, not the original one, so it becomes more severe as the cairn gets taller.

## Finding the Origin (Rule C4)
To reverse a pulse and find what height produced a given result, you solve the pulse equation backwards. This is unique—every final height can only come from one specific starting height. You undo pulses one at a time, working backwards from the final state.

## Drains (Rule C5)
A drain removes a fixed amount each cycle. A cairn keeps growing if each pulse adds more than the drain removes, but eventually the drain overtakes the pulse gains. You must cycle through each round, as the pulse bonus changes with height even though the drain stays constant.

## Merging (Rule C6)
Combining two cairns uses weighted shares (expressed in tenths) and a tether value. Each cairn contributes a fractional amount based on its share, those fractions are rounded to the nearest whole number, then the tether is applied as an adjustment. The shares alone don't determine the result—the tether is essential.
